To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) H2O2 induces nuclear PAR formation, 2) PKCα is required for H2O2-mediated PAR formation, 3) HMGB1 antagonizes PKCα-mediated PAR formation, and 4) H2O-induced PAR formation is mediated by PKCα-dependent Ca2+-dependent oxidative DNA damage and PKCα-independent Ca2+-dependent HMGB1 inhibition.
the PLC/IP3/Ca2+/ PKCα signaling axis controls the formation of PAR in the nucleus in response to H2O2.
PKCα is a positive regulator of H2O2-mediated PAR formation, while HMGB1 acts as a negative regulator of PAR formation, and both PKCα and HMBG1 are required for PAR formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the signaling pathways involved in the control of poly-ADP ribosylation in response to oxidative damage.
the molecular mechanisms that control the formation of poly ADP ribose, a posttranslational modification that is induced by oxidative stress and has been associated with cell death.
the molecular basis of the response of the cell to oxidative stress and how it is regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLC/IP3/Ca2+/HMGB1/PKCα signaling pathway is essential for H2O2-mediated poly-ADP ribosylation, but the exact mechanism is yet to be determined.
the PKCα-dependent activation of HMGB1 is required for the H2O2-mediated induction of nuclear PAR formation.

H2O2-mediated oxidative stress activates the PLC/IP3/Ca2+ signaling axis, which in turn activates PKCα and triggers the release of HMGB1 from chromatin to allow PAR formation in the nucleus, thereby contributing to the cellular response to oxidative stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
H2O2 induces PAR formation via a PKCα and Ca2+-dependent mechanism, and that PKCα antagonizes the inhibitory effect on PAR formation of the chromatin-modifying protein HMGA1.
PKCα is a key signaling molecule that is required to induce poly-ADP ribosylation (PAR) formation in response to H2O2.

PKCα and the chromatin structure modifying protein HMGB1 antagonize each other in the control of H2O2 induced PAR formation, and that PKCα is required to release HMGB1-mediated inhibition of PAR formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the balance between the PKCα and HMG1 signaling axes is crucial in regulating the cellular response to oxidative stress, and that the loss of this balance may be an important factor in oxidative stress-associated pathologies.
PKCα and the chromatin-associated protein HMGB1 antagonize each other in controlling the formation of nuclear poly-ADP ribose in response to oxidative damage.
